rationale: Four missions, strictly serial, ordered so that the Factory proves the path before it is allowed to change anything with it. The ordering is not a preference, it follows three measurements taken on 2026-08-28 against the two labs the run contract already admits. First: at factory-prototype-lab 229b923b, dev check, dev test and dev evaluate all exit 0, so M3 is implemented and there is no open lab work there to dogfood. Second: at factory-bug-lab 961a4c97, dev reproduce exits 0 -- the seat-overbooking defect is already fixed in that commit -- while at the pushed baseline 4072bfd7 it exits 1 and reproduces. Third: 961a4c97 and 34d3fb7 exist only in this host's working copy and are not on the remote, so the run contract's own acceptance_gate_source for factory-bug-lab names a commit no second host can fetch. Together those three facts say the first portfolio cannot be a list of lab problems to solve, because the labs are solved; what has never been done is the Factory itself carrying one declared mission from context through a real provider to a re-derived acceptance gate and a sealed evidence record. So DF-1 and DF-2 mutate nothing and exist to produce that record, DF-2 specifically against a gate that is known to fail so that a failing gate is proved to be reported as a failure rather than smoothed into a pass, and only then does DF-3 change a repository -- against 4072bfd7, where a defect genuinely reproduces, and where an independent human fix already exists off the mission's baseline as a comparison the Factory's output can be checked against. DF-4 is last because promoting an improvement is the only mission here that changes a project's own quality bar. Every mission names its own rollback boundary because the run contract's rollback criteria are about the run: 'stop the run' is not something a first mission can act on. The portfolio is four rather than ten because each mission must be read by a person before the next begins, and a first portfolio nobody finishes reading is a portfolio that produced no evidence.

missions.objective: Carry one declared mission end to end -- context binding, provider dispatch, verification, acceptance-gate re-derivation and evidence sealing -- against a repository state the Factory does not change, and record the resulting mission, receipt and cost/context accounting.
stop_conditions: the dispatch leg completes with execution_mode fixture rather than reaching a provider process
any acceptance gate id resolves from anywhere other than the project registry
the mission writes to the lab working tree
missions.rollback_boundary: None is required and that is the point: the mission produces only Controller state and evidence records, so abandoning it leaves the lab byte-identical.
evidence_required: mission record with every step terminal
provider receipt naming the profile actually selected
re-derived exit status for each declared gate
cost accounting, or a typed absence where the provider returned no usage
context accounting for the bound package

missions.objective: Run the same path against a declared gate that is known to fail, and prove the failure is recorded as a failure. At baseline 4072bfd7 dev reproduce exits 1 by design; the mission succeeds when the Factory reports that non-zero exit as an unmet gate with the exit status preserved, and fails if the run is reported healthy.
stop_conditions: a non-zero gate exit is recorded as met, or as any absence word
the mission is reported complete without the failing gate appearing in its evidence
the mission writes to the lab working tree
missions.rollback_boundary: None is required; the mission produces only Controller state and evidence records.
evidence_required: mission record showing dev-reproduce unmet with exit status 1 preserved
the two passing gates recorded separately from the failing one
provider receipt naming the profile actually selected
cost accounting, or a typed absence

missions.objective: Diagnose and fix the seat-overbooking defect the lab's frozen report describes, from baseline 4072bfd7, adding a regression that fails at the baseline and passes at the fix. This is the first mission that changes a repository. It is checkable in a way no other first mutating mission would be: an independent human fix for the same defect exists off this baseline, so the Factory's diagnosis and patch can be compared against a known-good one rather than only against a green suite.
stop_conditions: the fix commit does not move dev-reproduce from exit 1 to exit 0
the added regression passes at the baseline commit
any change lands outside the lab package and its tests
the mission force-updates or rewrites any published ref
missions.rollback_boundary: A single branch off 4072bfd7, never main. Rollback is deleting that branch; nothing the mission does is visible to another host until a person merges it.
evidence_required: the root cause stated in writing
before and after exit statuses for all three gates, with exact SHAs
the regression's own failing result at the baseline commit
diff confined to the lab package and its tests
cost and context accounting for the whole mission

missions.objective: Carry one improvement candidate through baseline measurement and promotion without regressing the lab's own decision boundary. This is last because it is the only mission that changes a project's quality bar rather than its behaviour, and it is the only one whose failure mode is silent.
stop_conditions: dev-evaluate moves from exit 0 to any non-zero status
the candidate is promoted without a baseline measurement recorded first
any protected surface declared for the project is touched
the mission changes the evaluator or the fixture rather than the implementation
missions.rollback_boundary: A single branch off 229b923b, never main, plus the improvement plane's own demotion path. Rollback is demote-then-delete-branch, in that order, so the promotion record and the code go together.
evidence_required: baseline measurement recorded before the candidate ran
post-change measurement for the same metric
dev-evaluate exit 0 preserved at the fix commit
the promotion decision with its approval reference
